outcome: Transfer to the neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: 878 consecutive twin pregnancies delivering two live births from a level-III university hospital maternity ward between 1997-2013 were included, excluding monoamniotic pregnancies, major congenital abnormalities, twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome, patients with missing gestational weight gain data in the last month before delivery, and patients with a BMI <=18.5.
finding: Adequate gestational weight gain in twin pregnancies was associated with better maternal (lower rates of preeclampsia and gestational hypertension) and neonatal outcomes (lower rates of preterm delivery, low birth weight, respiratory distress syndrome, NICU transfer, and better Apgar scores) compared to low or excessive gestational weight gain, supporting the appropriateness of IOM guidelines.
